thread.title: Hurry up — you’ve only got a couple of weeks to return holiday gifts from some retailers - MarketWatch

author: Alessandra Malito
title: Hurry up — you’ve only got a couple of weeks to return holiday gifts from some retailers - MarketWatch
text:
Holiday shopping may be a distant memory, but consumers are still busy. Return season started earlier than ever this year and is just hitting its stride.
Consumers spent more than $850 billion this holiday season — the strongest year in six years — according to Mastercard MA, +1.21% , but 13% of purchases (or $90 billion worth) will be returned, according to liquidation company B-Stock . And for the first time since United Parcel Service started tracking returns, the shipping company saw a surge in returns before Christmas: UPS UPS, +1.19% expected a record 1.5 million returns on Dec. 19, and anticipated another 1.3 million on Jan. 3 (in addition to another million every day of December).
About one-third (32%) of shoppers consider return policies when making their holiday purchases, according to the National Retail Federation , along with free shipping and sales or discounts. Almost six in 10 people say they plan to return or exchange unwanted gifts — 34% will probably do so within the first month, compared to 3% who plan to return or exchange items more than a month later and 21% who want to return gifts immediately, according to the NRF.
See: These are 4 of the biggest holiday stressors — and ways to cope
Some stores extend their return policies for holiday shoppers and giftees, but not all companies are so lenient. Here’s a list of stores and their return windows this holiday season:
Amazon AMZN, -0.63% : Items shipped between Nov. 1 and Dec. 31 can be returned until Jan. 31 for a full refund .
Apple AAPL, -0.65% : Purchases made online and received between Nov. 14 and Dec. 25 may be returned through Jan. 8. Purchases made after Dec. 25 are subject to standard return policy , which is 14 calendar days from the date received. Only products purchased directly through Apple can be returned to Apple stores.
Best Buy BBY, +0.76% : Almost all purchases made between Oct. 27 and Dec. 28 can be returned through Jan. 12, except cell phones, devices that can be activated and AppleCare monthly plans. Best Buy Elite members have until Jan. 27 to return or exchange products bought during the same timeframe, and Best Buy Elite Plus members have until Feb. 11.
DICK’s Sporting Goods DKS, -2.25% : Items bought at DICK’s Sporting Goods, Golf Galaxy and Field & Stream can be returned within 60 days .
GameStop GME, -1.77% : New merchandise , except tablets and accessories, can be returned for a full refund within 30 days if unopened (opened products are not eligible for refunds, but they can be exchanged for an identical product). Pre-owned merchandise must be returned within seven days of purchase.
Gap, Old Navy and Banana Republic GPS, +1.24% : Purchases can be returned up to 45 days after purchase. Unwanted gifts can be returned, exchanged or traded in for a gift card (which can be used for Gap, Old Navy, Banana Republic, Athleta and Hill City purchases).
Home Depot HD, +1.21% : Most new, unopened merchandise can be returned within 90 days, though there are exclusions, including furniture, mattresses and area rugs, which must be returned within 30 days.
Kmart: Products purchased between Nov. 1 and Dec. 24 can be returned through Jan. 31.
Kohl’s KSS, -1.67% : Kohl’s can locate purchases made on major credit cards for up to 16 months after date of purchase, so shoppers don’t necessarily have to show a receipt when they make a return. The company is offering a special holiday return policy , which allows premium electronics bought between Nov. 1 and Dec. 25 to be returned by Jan. 31 (usually there’s a 30-day return window).
Macy’s M, -0.30% : Most merchandise can be returned within 180 days of purchase, though some exclusions apply (including items marked “Last Act”).
Microsoft MSFT, +0.62% : Eligible items bought between Oct. 27 and Dec. 31 can be returned through Jan. 31.
Nike NKE, +0.96% : Orders placed between Nov. 1 and Jan. 14 have a 60-day return period.
Also see: Do you secretly visit McDonald’s or quietly shop at Louis Vuitton? Why guilty pleasures are so hard to give up
Sears SHLDQ, +7.81% : Most items purchased between Nov. 1 and Dec. 25 can be returned by Jan. 31. Certain products, including vacuum cleaners, major home appliances and items with less-than-30-day return windows, are not eligible. Christmas decor cannot be returned after Dec. 25.
Target TGT, -0.60% : Electronics and entertainment items purchased between Nov. 1 and Dec. 25 must be returned within 30 days of Dec. 26 for a refund or exchange. Otherwise , most unopened items in new condition can be returned or exchanged within 90 days. Apple products, excluding phones, bought between Nov. 1 and Dec. 25 must be returned within 15 days of Dec. 26.
Walmart WMT, +1.31% : Some orders placed between Oct. 28 and Dec. 25 have extended return deadlines. Items that typically have a 15-day return window can be returned by Jan. 10, whereas those that have a 30-day return window can be returned by Jan. 25. The return window for products with a 90-day timeframe remains unchanged .
(None of the retailers listed in this story responded immediately to requests for comment.)
